column4: componentize-py and wasm-tools are not installed on this runner, and these four tests need a real Python guest: they drive a pending child await through the component boundary and observe whether the guest runs on, which only executing one can show. Whole tests with no dialect arm, so the job's DSNs do not change the count. Declared under all four keys that reject a new ./engine/ toolchain skip -- multi-db/mysql, multi-db/mssql, cluster, and test-go/engine (the last required by scripts/check-skips.sh's pairing rule; engine-race.yml is scheduled and does not run on PRs, so that count is the rule applied, not a reading of its report). Same mechanism as the sibling TestPythonGuest tests, measured on cleat#3432's multi-db/mysql, multi-db/mssql and cluster job reports. NOT yet measured on this PR's own jobs; CI is the first reading. (cleat#3429) CORRECTED after the first CI run on this PR: the fifth test, TestPythonGuestPendingChildAwaitStopsTheGuestBeforeItsNextSideEffect, loops two entries with t.Run, so it skips as two SUBTESTS while its parent reports PASS; it is declared on its own line.

The two subtests of TestPythonGuestPendingChildAwaitStopsTheGuestBeforeItsNextSideEffect (await_child_pending, await_all_children_pending): the parent test loops its entries with t.Run and each subtest skips on the missing toolchain (componentize-py/wasm-tools) while the parent reports PASS, so the skip names carry the /subtest suffix and the whole-test regex cannot match them. Measured on this PR's own first CI run: the Skip budget step of Test MySQL, Test SQL Server and Cluster Integration Tests named exactly these as the 2 skips matching no ledger line. The test-go/engine count is the pairing rule applied, not a reading of engine-race.yml. (cleat#3429)
